sources.title: US Department of State, Office of the Historian: The Chinese Revolution of 1949
sources.note: Original institutional history directly read. Japanese surrender, renewed civil war, proclamation of PRC on 1 October 1949 and Nationalist retreat to Taiwan. Retired historical series, not used for current policy.

sources.title: Congressional Research Service, China Primer: China’s Political System, IF12505
sources.note: Official original HTML version dated 3 January 2025 directly read. Party-state, hierarchy, State Council, legislature, propaganda and security oversight. Later April 2026 version located on EveryCRSReport but only stable institutional features used; no current officeholder counts. All IF12505 versions form one work.

sources.title: Xin Meng, Nancy Qian and Pierre Yared, The Institutional Causes of China’s Great Famine, 1959 to 1961
sources.note: Original NBER working paper 16361, abstract and indexed printed page 9 read. Direct PDF returned 403. Original indexed section covers 1958 communal kitchens, production decline, excessive state procurement and famine mortality. Used without asserting a single exact death toll.

sources.title: Library of Congress, Eliminate the four old, establish the four new, poster (1967)
sources.note: Original object catalogue directly read. Canton, 1967; Red Guard youths destroying old traditions; catalogue describes religion, literature, capitalism and imperialism. Full image restricted to onsite access. This is a propaganda object, not proof everyone acted as depicted.

sources.title: John Giles, Albert Park and Meiyan Wang, The Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution, Disruptions to Education, and Returns to Schooling in Urban China (2008)
sources.note: Library of Congress catalogue reproduces the World Bank original study abstract: city-wide educational disruption during 1966 to 1976; variation across cohorts. No regression findings or quantified returns used.

sources.title: Bert Hofman, Reflections on forty years of China’s reforms, World Bank (2018)
sources.note: Original institutional author account and chronological annex read. 1978 reform turning point, household responsibility, township/village enterprises, special economic zones in 1980. Same underlying work as linked PDF.

sources.title: World Bank, From Poor Areas to Poor People: China’s Evolving Poverty Reduction Agenda (2009)
sources.note: Original indexed printed page 78: household responsibility system granted farm households land-use rights and residual output after grain-delivery and tax obligations. No inference of private land ownership.

sources.title: National Security Archive, Tiananmen Massacre 30th Anniversary (4 June 2019)
sources.note: Original archival exhibit directly read, linking declassified documentary collections. Armed attacks on protesters, military massacre and official suppression of historical discussion. No unsupported exact casualty count or claim all killings occurred inside the square.

sources.title: Chinese Posters, New Marriage Law (1950)
sources.note: IISH/Landsberger collection contextual essay directly read: law promulgated 1 May 1950; free choice, monogamy, legal equality, registration, implementation disputes. Used as collection scholarship, not as proof a campaign achieved universal equality.

sources.title: International Institute of Social History, Support the marriage law, BG C15/751 (1950)
sources.note: Original collection catalogue directly read. Designer Sha; 1950; 39 by 27 cm; IISH collection. Catalogue supplies 拥护婚姻法, Yonghu hunyinfa and English title; notes husband and wife shaking hands and 27 articles on reverse. Image request failed, so writing explicitly a catalogue transcription in modern characters, not a visual palaeographic verification. IISH record https://search.iisg.amsterdam/Record/1074204.

sources.title: UNFPA China, The solution to shifting fertility rates lies in prioritizing the reproductive rights of all people (11 July 2021)
sources.note: Original report directly read: universal two-child policy in 2016 and three-child policy announced May 2021; rights-based reproductive policy argument. A dated account, not current individualized legal guidance.

sources.title: UNICEF China, A grandmother’s journey raising left-behind children (13 February 2026)
sources.note: Original directly read. Zhang Qin in rural Guizhou raises grandchildren while son and daughter-in-law work in Jiangsu; video calls and caregiving support. Article dated 2026, photos dated 2025; use article date explicitly and avoid national extrapolation.

sources.title: UNESCO, Spring festival, social practices of the Chinese people in celebration of traditional new year (2024 inscription)
sources.note: Original element account read. Cleaning/provisions before festival, family reunion dinner and staying up, greetings and intergenerational transmission. Longstanding practices documented in a contemporary nomination, not invented in 2024.

sources.title: UNESCO, Traditional tea processing techniques and associated social practices in China (2022 inscription)
sources.note: Original element account read. Six categories including green, white, oolong and black; guest hospitality; families and apprenticeships; pastries. Not a claim all regions or households prepare the same tea.

sources.title: UNICEF China, Children bring revolutions to their schools (22 June 2009)
sources.note: Original directly read. Doujiang Primary School, Sanjiang County, Guangxi: My Voice bulletin and student requests, sports equipment managed by students. Teacher-centred to child-centred changes are programme examples, not national outcomes.

sources.title: UNICEF China, It’s all about children thriving (2023)
sources.note: Original report directly read. August 2023 visit to Taizi Township Central School, Huzhu Tu Autonomous County, Qinghai: cold-weather toilets, solar heated handwashing water, partitions, more female stalls and accessible room. Related health-centre installations distinguished from school.

sources.title: Cui Weiyuan, China’s village doctors take great strides, Bulletin of the WHO 86(12), December 2008
sources.note: Original indexed printed page 914 read. Short-term training, village-based prevention and treatment, combination of farming and health work; 1960s barefoot doctor scheme and 1980s examination-based village doctor designation.

sources.title: Tu Youyou, Nobel Prize biographical account (2015)
sources.note: Scientist’s first-person account, original indexed text read; direct HTML returned 403. 4 October 1971 extract no.191, 1972 clinical work, 1972 isolation, collaboration, and 1973 tablets that failed to disintegrate followed by capsules. The Chinese term 青蒿素 and translation artemisinin appear explicitly. No self-medication instructions or suggestion crude herbal tea is equivalent.

sources.title: Martha Lawrence, Richard Bullock and Ziming Liu, China’s High-Speed Rail Development (World Bank, 2019)
sources.note: Original indexed printed page 12 checked: more than 25,000 route-km by end-2017; graph includes mixed-use lines at 200 kph. Report overview and original authorship verified in World Bank catalogue. No current network total asserted.

sources.title: Chinese Academy of Sciences, International payload laser retroreflector deployed on Moon’s far side by Chang’e-6 (25 June 2024)
sources.note: Original research institution report read. Landing 2 June and return capsule 25 June 2024; first far-side sample return; INRRI jointly developed with INFN Frascati; reflector mounted on lander.

sources.title: Chinese Academy of Sciences, Chang’e-6 sample studies cast light on the Moon’s far side (18 November 2024)
sources.note: Original institutional report of Nature research indexed text checked. Samples show volcanic episodes around 2.8 and 4.2 billion years ago. Combined conservatively with 2024 mission report as one mission-work group.

sources.title: World Bank, Lifting 800 million people out of poverty (1 April 2022)
sources.note: Original joint World Bank/Chinese institutional report release read. Close to 800 million reduction over forty years at the then-used $1.90/day international poverty line. Threshold/date explicit; not the disappearance of all hardship.

sources.title: World Trade Organization, Accessions: China
sources.note: Original accession record checked; member from 11 December 2001. No sovereignty inference from separate customs-territory memberships.

proposedOverrides.name: China
proposedOverrides.summary: China’s post-1945 history spans civil war, the People’s Republic, profound social change and continuing political conflict.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact ID only. Distinguish Republic of China in 1945 from PRC founded 1 October 1949; do not associate Taiwan, Tibet, Xinjiang, Manchuria or earlier Chinese dynasty records.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: 1945 to 1960 feature bbox [89.419,18.097,122.392,46.752]; 1960 and later mainland feature bbox [73.677,18.097,134.719,53.51]. world-2010 additionally attaches a separately labelled Hong Kong polygon [113.835,22.172,114.415,22.561]. These broad snapshots are not precise civil-war fronts or sovereignty adjudications.
batchIdentityNotes.intervalNote: Final exclusive end 2027 only displays dated material through 2026; not an end prediction.
